Conclusion


        Many of the important BAASS projects, including Northern Tier, entry into classified archives, Project Oral History, as well as contacting key people in the military and private sector are on hold because BAASS currently does not have the Need to Know for this information. BAASS in collaboration with the sponsor has recently taken tentative steps to contact some organizations within the USG that may have access to material and archives. These contacts are at much too a preliminary stage to assess the likelihood of their success or failure.

        In spite of the above impediments, significant progress has been made in training and initially deploying BAASS field investigative teams during the fall 2009 months. A large part of the current investigations at BAASS are focused on the Utah ranch and surrounding areas. The BAASS MUFON relationship is being closely monitored especially since the case numbers that MUFON are alerting BAASS with, although improving, are still lower than originally expected. The BAASS database of cases is now larger than any other database owned by UAP organizations in North America. It should be noted that BAASS has initiated a separate Capella database for the events on the Utah ranch and surrounding areas, a report on which will be forthcoming in the coming months.
